newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy insurer Generali sets up Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Italy insurer Generali sets up Holocaust fund.

text.p: Italian insurance company Generali said it had set up a $12 million fund to honour victims of the Holocaust following controversy over policies held by Jews before World War Two.

A company statement on Tuesday night said the money would be spent over 12 years to support organisations engaged in perpetuating the memory of Holocaust victims and for cultural and charitable purposes.

Generali, however, stood by its position that it could not be held responsible for claims from relatives of victims of Nazi Germany's campaign to exterminate Jews on policies they held in eastern Europe.

The decision to create the fund "does not regard in any way the requests for compensation advanced by the heirs of citizens of Jewish origin insured with Generali before the Second World War in countries of central and eastern Europe", it said.
Generali had a dominant share of the insurance market in eastern Europe before World War Two.
It says all its businesses in the region were expropriated and nationalised after 1945 by the communist governments which took power and that it cannot therefore be held liable.
The company is one of seven European insurance firms against which a massive U.S. lawsuit was filed in March.
The class action suit, combining the claims of an estimated 10,000 plaintiffs, accuses the seven firms of cheating Holocaust victims of billions of dollars.
Generali has also run into criticism in Israel, including last week from the finance committee of parliament.

The company earlier this year invested $320 million to acquire a majority stake in Israeli insurer Migdal, the insurance arm of Israeli government-owned Bank Leumi, and has faced threats of a boycott.

Tuesday's statement said Generali had initially intended to announce the Holocaust fund in July during a planned visit to Israel by its chairman Antoine Bernheim and managing director Gianfranco Gutty.

Generali had decided to bring the announcement forward to "make the feelings of the company known on the problem in question" following what the statement said were false reports that had circulated after the finance committee meeting.

"By investing $320 million in Israel to purchase the majority of Migdal stock...Generali has demonstrated that it believes strongly in the peace process and in the outlook for the Israeli economy," the statement said.
